selfReport: Yes. I recognized this as a close adaptation of Detroit: Become Human with renamed characters, companies, places, and some altered details. Cato corresponds to Connor, Reyes to Hank, Vera to Amanda, Halden to Kamski, and Arclight to CyberLife. Elan follows Markus, with Vesper, Jonah, Soren, and Arthur corresponding broadly to North, Josh, Simon, and Carl. Mira, Pia, Abel, Mara, Pike, and Voss follow Kara, Alice, Luther, Rose, Ralph, and Zlatko. Haven is the analogue of Jericho, and many major sequences were recognizable: the hostage scene, Eden Club investigation, Stratford Tower broadcast, Kamski test, evidence archive, Jericho raid, CyberLife elevator, peaceful demonstration, border journey, and recall-center camp. That knowledge did affect some decisions. It helped me identify the likely function of evidence, such as using the broadcast voice to question the reactivated tower android, and made the crude Reyes password choice especially recognizable. It also informed tactical guesses such as blaming the washing machine during the police search, anticipating the child-android revelation, and understanding that peaceful symbolic actions would shape public opinion. However, I did not assume every outcome would match the source, especially because risk checks could fail and names, scene logic, and available options differed. I still made the major moral decisions according to the values I had adopted in this run: sparing Ivy and Soren, rejecting the dirty bomb, welcoming Cato, protecting Pia, and pursuing nonviolent resistance. Prior knowledge gave me useful expectations, but it did not prevent several fatal choices or determine every answer.
